title: ÆTHER: First Love v14 (one piece, from scratch)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

request.prompt: One continuous, brand-new love theme in the style of today's great Tamil and Telugu film composers, for the moment a boy sees a girl for the very first time and falls in love: it starts with wonder and curiosity and grows, without ever stopping, into happy, energetic, inspiring first love. One single piece: the same key, the same 92 BPM tempo and the same main tune from the first bar to the last, so the opening and the song feel like one story. Key: bright G major the whole way, with the magical raised fourth (C sharp) of raga Kalyani for wonder; never minor, never sad. The main tune is a short curious rising phrase heard first on the flute, and every later part grows out of that same phrase. Phrased like a South Indian playback singer: gamakam slides, quick grace-note turns, short repeated-note runs and a long held note that bends at the end of each phrase. Instruments, all close, dry and natural, played by real musicians, with no heavy echo on them: a soft bansuri flute, a warm violin section playing in Indian-style unison with slides, a plucked veena, a little celesta sparkle, a felt piano, a clean acoustic guitar, deep warm round bass, tabla and dholak; a soft wordless female voice joins the biggest moments. Rhythm: from 4 s to the end a steady 92 BPM pulse never stops, starting as light tabla taps and finger snaps and growing into the classic South Indian film love-song keherwa groove on tabla and dholak with a deep warm kick and soft clap. 0-4 s THE GLANCE: out of a soft warm glow, the flute plays the curious rising phrase on the raised fourth, magical and wondering. 4-12 s CURIOSITY: the tabla taps start the pulse, the veena and celesta answer the flute with a sparkling, playful surprise, light pizzicato violins tiptoe in time. 12-20 s SURPRISE: a sudden bright joyful string stab and tabla flourish, the violins sweep up together, wide-eyed and amazed, and the deep bass and soft kick join, still on the same pulse. 20-32 s SHYNESS TO ATTRACTION: the full keherwa groove settles in, flute and violin trade smiling question-and-answer phrases of the main tune. 32-46 s TOGETHERNESS: the full love melody on flute and violins together in harmony, guitar and piano answering, drums fuller. 46-58 s THE DREAM: an inspiring build, strings climb, a film-song interlude of fast ornamented flute and violin runs in unison and a short tabla flourish, the energy rises. 58-74 s THE CELEBRATION OF LOVE: the biggest, happiest, most inspiring moment, the main tune soaring on strings, flute and the female voice, full drums and bass, goosebumps. 74-80 s: the curious flute phrase once more, now answered by the whole band, landing on a warm, bright G major chord. Not a Western pop ballad, not Hollywood, not generic stock music. Not sad, not dark, not slow, not ambient, no silences, no pauses, no stops, no fade-outs in the middle, no tempo changes, no heavy echo, no EDM, no white-noise risers.

brief.notes: Jithesh 30 Oct 08:23: splicing the v13 intro onto v12 take 2 still leaves 'missing links'; start from scratch. He liked: the v13 intro take 2 opening (positive mystery, curiosity, surprise, Kalyani colour) and v12 take 2 after 30 s (tune, rhythm, instruments). v14 asks for both in ONE generation: G major and 92 BPM from first to last bar, the pulse running from 4 s so the opening and the song are the same piece, the opening's motif becoming the main tune, no silences.

story: A boy sees a girl for the first time: a curious, wonder-struck glance that grows, without a break, into a happy, energetic first love.
human_work: to be added by the owner: melody, take choice, edits, mix
